title: Galatasaray banned from selling away tickets for Champions League tie at Liverpool
content:
There will be no Galatasaray supporters in the Anfield away end for the Champions League last-16 decider against Liverpool after the Turkish club was hit with a UEFA sanction.

The European governing body has banned Galatasaray for selling tickets to its supporters for one away match for the “throwing of objects, lighting of fireworks and crowd disturbances” during their 3-2 defeat at Juventus on February 25. The Turkish club have also been fined €40,000 (£34.7k) as part of the ruling by UEFA’s Appeals Body.

In a statement, Galatasaray said it would appeal against UEFA’s decision.

Travelling supporters of the Super Lig side set off flares and fireworks in the away end at Juventus’ Allianz Stadium last month.

According to local media reporting in Italy, Galatasaray fans clashed with home supporters and local police before the game, and a father and daughter were taken to hospital for checks after being hit by a firecracker thrown from the away end.

Despite losing to ten-man Juventus in Turin in the play-off round decider, Burak Okan’s side progressed to the knockouts with a 7-5 win on aggregate.

Liverpool visit Istanbul for the first leg of the last-16 tie on March 10 before the second leg back on Merseyside eight days later.
